maria: Heads-up — we need a short decision about the benchmark harness for the upcoming perf round. Replay vs synthetic comparison: how do we make it apples-to-apples given kernel selection and KV cache effects?

sam: +1. My gut: deterministic replay with controlled inter-arrival times, plus a synthetic profile that matches the same seq-len/batch distribution. record RNG seeds and traffic clock.

ki: Important to record which kernel the runtime picks per request. Kernel selection changes with batch size & seq length — if that flips between runs we won't be comparing like-for-like. Suggest we snapshot kernel choices and force a fixed kernel set for the direct comparisons.

maria: Agree. Also KV cache warmup matters a lot for goodput and tail. Replay will naturally have cache state but synthetic runs often start cold. We should run a warmup phase and capture cache hit/miss histograms.

perf-bot: automated note: last night’s nightly harness completed. baseline tokens/sec 12.3k, p95 TTFT 78ms, p99 220ms (model: opt-6.7b-q5) :white_check_mark:

jason: Quick ask — can someone write down exact metric defs so we all use the same language? I keep seeing TTFT/TPOT/goodput/QPS used inconsistently.

elaine: Short defs we can use in test docs: TTFT = time from request accept to first token emitted at client (includes routing + kernel startup). TPOT = median time per output token over steady-state generation (exclude first token). QPS = requests started/second. Goodput = useful tokens/sec (tokens that are actually consumed by client) — excludes retries and 0-token system responses.

sam: Add: measure TPOT both as instantaneous token throughput and as an amortized steady-state number; report both mean and p95/p99. For batching, report effective batch size distribution and kernel mapping.

ki: We should also report "kernel-switch rate" (fraction of requests where chosen kernel differs across runs) and a KV-cache-hit-rate curve by prefix length. This explains a lot of variance.

maria: Proposed minimal harness plan: 1) deterministic replay with recorded timestamps + cache state replayed where possible, 2) synthetic generator seeded to match seq-len & pause distributions, 3) warmup window to reach steady-state cache and batch patterns, 4) collect per-request kernel id, batch size, TTFT, per-token times, kv hit/miss tag, and traffic seed.

maria: config snippet for the synthetic run (example):
```yaml
generator:
  seed: 123456
  distribution:
    seq_length: {p10: 8, p50: 64, p90: 512}
  pause_ms: {mean: 20, stddev: 5}
warmup_seconds: 120
record_kernel_choices: true
collect_kv_histogram: true
```

sam: Looks good. For apples-to-apples, we should also run a variant where kernel selection is pinned (i.e., force the same kernel as baseline) so we can measure kernel-induced delta vs other factors.

elaine: For regression gating, propose: fail if p95 TTFT increases > 10% AND goodput drops > 5% at same config. Flag for manual triage if kernel-switch-rate > 1%.

ki: Data collection notes — include per-core GPU utilization, memcpy time, kernel launch latencies, and KV cache lookup latencies. These help pinpoint whether batching or KV lookups are introducing the tail.

perf-bot: acknowledged. I will add new metrics to nightly JSON output: kernel_id[], batch_hist[], kv_hit_rate_by_prefix[], rng_seed, ttft_ms_p50_p95_p99, tpottoken_ms_stats, goodput_tokens_per_sec.

maria: OK let's land this. Sam/ki — can you two prepare a short doc (one-pager) with the pinned-kernel vs normal runs and runbook for triage? Target EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:

sam: on it.

ki: will do, adding sample viz for kv hit curves.
